Findings.title: The reviewer is never given the commit messages, so the review path cannot check what it says it checks.
Findings.detail: Docs/REVIEW.md step 1 says the change must match its stated purpose, naming the commit messages first. AGENTS.md S-16 leaves commit messages to review, because the linter does not cover them. The script writes only changes.diff and files.txt to the input folder (lines 166-167). Review/reviewer-prompt.md lists only those two inputs. A git diff holds no commit messages, and the worktree is a detached checkout that the reviewer cannot run git against. So the reviewer cannot judge a commit message against the change, and a real host or account name in a message cannot be found. The review also overstates its coverage of S-16 and of intent. Fix: write a commits.txt from git log of base..head into the input folder, and list it in the prompt.

Findings.title: Stack 6 is marked Complete (v0.2.6) while its own stage tasks are still open.
Findings.detail: STAGES.md now says Stack 6 is Complete, and the commit message says 'Stack 6 complete in STAGES'. Docs/TODO.md in the same commit still has the Stack 6 tasks 'Take one pull request through the full path with findings attached' and 'Closing tasks' unticked. The stage goal in TODO.md is a review path shown working on one real pull request, and no real PR has gone through it: the audit record covers a discarded plant. The document states something the repository state contradicts. Tick the tasks first, or leave the stage as in progress.
